name: Truist Financial
description: Truist is a Charlotte-based bank holding company with $547.5B of assets and $400.4B of deposits, operating 1,927 branches through Truist Bank. It earns most of its revenue from the spread between loan and deposit rates (net interest income $14.4B versus $5.9B of fees) across consumer, small business and wholesale clients. Wholesale Banking earns more (segment net income $4.1B) than Consumer and Small Business Banking ($2.5B), and a large corporate/treasury bucket swings the total. It sold its insurance brokerage, Truist Insurance Holdings, in 2024, which is why 2024 and 2025 figures are on a continuing-operations basis.

businessLines.name: Consumer and Small Business Banking
businessLines.how: Retail, premier and small-business clients pay interest on loans (indirect auto, mortgage, card, other consumer) and fees for checking, payments and mortgage; the segment earns a funds-transfer-pricing credit on the deposits it gathers, which is 82 percent of its revenue (9,584 of 11,657, computed).

revenue.note: Segment net interest income 9,584 (after funds-transfer-pricing credit on deposits) plus noninterest income 2,073

businessLines.revenueNote: Segment net interest income 9,584 (after funds-transfer-pricing credit on deposits) plus noninterest income 2,073

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), segment net income from continuing operations

businessLines.name: Wholesale Banking
businessLines.how: Commercial, corporate, institutional and wealth clients pay interest on loans and deposit spread plus fees for treasury management, card, investment banking, wealth advisory and lending; 38 percent of segment revenue is noninterest income (4,164 of 10,824, computed) and its income includes tax-credit investments grossed up to a pre-tax equivalent.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), segment net income from continuing operations

businessLines.name: Other, Treasury & Corporate
businessLines.how: Not a customer business: securities portfolio, most long-term debt, hedging derivatives, liquidity and funding, and corporate functions; 2024 carried a large securities loss from a balance sheet repositioning.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), net loss from continuing operations

brands.name: Truist Insurance Holdings (TIH)
brands.note: Insurance brokerage, sold in 2024 and reported as discontinued operations (2024 net income from discontinued operations to common shareholders 4,863M).
